VR.1.1.1.note: Second review. Correct as it stands. Vyākhyā: five connected sentences, a real retelling and no longer a word list; अर्थात् twice (वाग्विदां वरः, परिपप्रच्छ), both on hard words; every sentence grammatical; anusvāra only before consonants; nothing added except पुरा and मुनिः as connective context; all bold words are the verse's own (तपसि, स्वाध्याये, निरतः, वरः, मुनिपुङ्गवः correctly re-inflected). Glosses: तपस्वी → तपः कुर्वन् and नारदम् → नारदनामकं मुनिम् are simpler and in the pada's case; the rest are unchanged and right. Padaccheda, analyses, vigrahas, anvaya, context note and speaker (null) are unchanged from the version passed before and remain correct.

VR.1.1.2.note: One small mechanical fix (लोके); everything else is right. Vyākhyā: natural and connected, अर्थात् twice (साम्प्रतम्, कृतज्ञः), grammar faultless (कः वीर्यवान् अस्ति, कः च धर्मज्ञः; न विस्मरति; स्वव्रतं च न त्यजति), pausal म् correct before the dashes, speaker named and linked to verse 1, nothing added. Glosses: नु → प्रश्नार्थकम् अव्ययम् follows the ruling; वीर्यवान् → बलवान्, शूरः is simpler; धर्मं जानन् etc. keep the pada's case. Padaccheda, analyses, vigrahas, anvaya, context note and speaker are unchanged and correct. FOR THE SCHOLAR (not a ruled point, applies to verses 2 and 3): च is now glossed अपि everywhere. In verse 4 that is exactly right (देवाः च = even the gods, च in the sense of अपि). In verses 2 and 3 च is the plain connective (समुच्चये). अपि can also mean 'and also', so the gloss is not wrong, but it is not simpler than च, it hides the real difference from verse 4, and a beginner who substitutes it gets कः अपि, which he has learnt as 'someone'. I recommend तथा for the connective च (or, on the model of the नु ruling, योजकम् अव्ययम्), keeping अपि only where च means 'even'. Also for the scholar: how far the bracket rule reaches. The draft brackets (तेषां), (कार्यं कर्तुं), (सर्वेषां), (ये स्वर्गे वसन्ति) but leaves उत्तमैः in उत्तमैः गुणैः युक्तः, सदा in सदा सत्यं वदन् and सम्यक् in verse 1 unbracketed; I read these as part of a natural paraphrase and have not counted them as faults. OPTIONAL: the first vyākhyā sentence has 11 words (§5.4 says 4–10; the checker allows 12) and three dashes in a row; अस्मिन् लोके साम्प्रतम् — अर्थात् इदानीम् — गुणवान् कः अस्ति ? reads more easily.

fixes.problem: §5.7: a word the gloss supplies beyond the pada stands in round brackets. The gloss repeats the pada and adds मनुष्याणाम्, which the word does not say (it is the same kind of addition as (सर्वेषां) in the ruling and as (ये स्वर्गे वसन्ति) under देवाः). The gloss itself is correct and helpful.

VR.1.1.2.round: fix round: the bracket fix was applied exactly as the reviewer prescribed (verified mechanically)

VR.1.1.3.note: No definite error. Vyākhyā: connected, अर्थात् twice (चारित्रेण युक्तः, सर्वभूतेषु हितः), all sentences grammatical, pausal म् right (शोभनम् ?), linked by पुनः and speaker named; the last sentence explains एकप्रियदर्शनः exactly as ruled, with (सर्वेषां) in brackets; विद्वान् and समर्थः are joined in one question, which is harmless. Glosses checked: चारित्रेण → शोभनेन आचरणेन (right, तृतीया); हितः → (तेषां) शुभं कुर्वन् (right, natural, प्रथमा); विद्वान् → बहु जानन्, ज्ञानी (right); समर्थः → यः (कार्यं कर्तुं) शक्नोति सः (right and clear; शक्तः would be shorter); एकप्रियदर्शनः as ruled. Padaccheda, analyses, vigrahas, anvaya, context note and speaker unchanged and correct. FOR THE SCHOLAR: (1) च → अपि, three times: here च is the plain connective, see the note on verse 2; I recommend तथा. (2) युक्तः → यस्य (तत्) अस्ति सः: correct in sense and formally in the pada's case, but awkward. The pada governs the instrumental चारित्रेण and the gloss cannot be put in its place, and (तत्) has nothing to point to when the entry is read alone. Recommended: (तेन) सहितः, which is everyday and keeps the instrumental. (3) Linga, all from memory, I could not open the kośas: चारित्र नपुं — I do not recall it in the Amarakośa; Apte gives चारित्रम् as neuter; confirmed on Apte. भूत in सर्वभूतेषु नपुं — as I recall, the Amarakośa nānārtha line (युक्ते क्ष्मादावृते भूतं प्राण्यतीते समे त्रिषु) gives the sense 'living being' as त्रिषु, that is, without a fixed gender, so the Amarakośa does not settle it; Apte gives भूतम् neuter for 'a being' and सर्वाणि भूतानि is the constant usage, so नपुं stands on Apte. The form भूतेषु does not show gender. The scholar should verify the Amarakośa line.
VR.1.1.3.round: the reviewer's two gloss recommendations (च → तथा, युक्तः → (तेन) सहितः) were adopted; the flag stands for the kośa check

VR.1.1.4.note: Correct as it stands. Vyākhyā: grammatical throughout (मनः स्ववशे भवति; सः क्रोधं जितवान्; क्रुद्धात् कस्मात् … भीताः भवन्ति with the ablative that the ruling's gloss requires); अर्थात् twice (अनसूयकः, and the restatement of the last question); nothing added, no name given to the man asked about; speaker named, linked by अन्यत् अपि. Glosses: आत्मवान् → यस्य मनः स्वस्य वशे अस्ति सः, द्युतिमान् → तेजस्वी (the commoner word), अनसूयकः → ईर्ष्यां न कुर्वन् …, बिभ्यति → भीताः भवन्ति, जातरोषस्य → क्रुद्धस्य … तस्य are all right and in the pada's case. देवाः → देवाः (ये स्वर्गे वसन्ति) is right and follows the ruling for an already simple word. च → अपि is right here: this च means 'even'. कस्य is षष्ठी with (कस्मात् इति अर्थः) as ruled. संयुग is now पुं as ruled (Amarakośa, from memory: it stands in the masculine list … कलिसंस्फोटसंयुगाः). अनसूयकः unhyphenated with vigraha न असूयकः as ruled. Anvaya has the supplied च in parentheses. OPTIONAL: in कस्य जातरोषस्य संयुगे देवाः अपि बिभ्यति the genitive stands next to संयुगे and can be read as 'in whose battle'; the order of the anvaya, संयुगे जातरोषस्य कस्य देवाः अपि बिभ्यति ?, avoids that. The explanatory statement तादृशस्य पुरुषस्य … जितवान् stands in the middle of Vālmīki's questions; it would sit better after them.

VR.1.1.5.note: Correct as it stands; both faults of the first review are gone. Vyākhyā: four sentences, अर्थात् once (कौतूहलम्), grammar faultless, हि in second place, anusvāra now only before consonants (परं कौतूहलम्, एवंविधं नरं ज्ञातुं) and म् before the vowel (कौतूहलम् अस्ति); एवंविधः नरः correctly re-inflected and explained by नाम; linked by एवं पृष्ट्वा, speaker named. Glosses: इच्छामि → इच्छां करोमि and ज्ञातुम् → ज्ञानं प्राप्तुम् are paraphrases, not rarer synonyms; कौतूहलम् → ज्ञातुम् इच्छा is प्रथमा एकवचन like the pada; हि → यतः (कारणं वदति) is right and helpful; महा-ऋषे → हे महामुने नारद, (सम्बोधनम्) has the prescribed form; अहम् (वाल्मीकिः), त्वम् (नारदः) bracketed correctly; नरम् → मनुष्यम् is fine. कौतूहल नपुं is confirmed by the Amarakośa (from memory: कौतूहलं कौतुकं च कुतुकं च कुतूहलम्). Padaccheda, analyses, vigrahas, anvaya, context note and speaker unchanged and correct. OPTIONAL: समर्थः → यः (ज्ञातुं) शक्नोति सः is right but sits oddly beside त्वम् … असि; शक्तः would do. असि → भवसि is a synonym of the same level, not a simpler word; it could simply be left as (त्वम्) असि. The first vyākhyā sentence has 11 words (§5.4 says 4–10; the checker allows 12).
